games.name: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap

components.label: Top-level task state machine with soft reset and sleep mode
components.summary: AgbMain runs one task handler per frame (TITLE, FILE_SELECT, GAME, GAMEOVER, STAFFROLL, DEBUG), then the message, fade and audio updates. The GAME task has its own transition/init/main/exit states and main sub-states (init room, change room, update, change area, Minish portal, barrel update, subtask). Pause menus, the kinstone menu, world-event reveals, map hints and fast travel run as subtasks inside GAME. Holding A+B+Select+Start soft-resets. The pause menu also offers sleep mode (GBA Stop), woken with L+R+Select.

components.label: Nintendo/Capcom logos, zooming-sword title and idle loop back to logos (no attract demo)
components.summary: Boot shows the Nintendo and Capcom logos (120-frame timer or key press). The USA title fades in the title BGM, zooms the Picori sword on an affine layer for 15 frames, holds 40 frames, then spawns the logo object for a 300-frame intro before showing a blinking PRESS START. A or Start (after fades) goes to file select. After 3600 idle frames (60 s) the sequence returns to the logos; the retail game has no gameplay attract demo (demo.c is a kiosk scenario picker compiled only into the USA demo build). The 60 s attract capture stayed on the title.

components.label: Three-slot file select with copy/erase, options and 6-character name entry
components.summary: File select lists 3 slots; empty slots open name entry, valid slots open a view with Start / Copy / Erase, R opens options (message speed, brightness). Name entry is a 13x6 character grid with page switching on L/R, B as backspace and Start jumping to END; names are up to 6 characters and cannot be empty. New files start with 3 hearts. The capture shows the name grid and a "Saving file..." dialog when the slot is created.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:keyframes f000670 (ENTER A NAME grid), f000820_scene (Saving file dialog)

components.label: Anywhere-save to mirrored, checksummed EEPROM records
components.summary: The player can save from the pause menu at any time (and at game over / after credits); loading resumes at the last recorded room-entry status. Saves go to 8 KiB EEPROM: a header plus three 0x500-byte slots, each written twice (primary and mirror at +0x1000) with status words (valid / untouched / deleted) and a two-part checksum; reads fall back to the mirror. Saving is a staged state machine that fades master volume out by 8 per frame, waits 8 frames, writes, then fades volume back in.

components.label: Game over with save prompt, continue at last entrance with 3 hearts
components.summary: When health reaches 0 (and no bottled fairy auto-revives), the game-over task fades in, raises the GAME OVER text, asks whether to save, then offers Continue or Quit. Continue reloads from the saved room status with health set to 24 units (3 hearts); Quit soft-resets.

components.label: Top-down 3/4 view with a z-height axis and two floor layers
components.summary: The world is a top-down grid of 16x16 px tiles (rooms up to 64 tiles wide) viewed at a slight 3/4 angle. Entities have a separate z coordinate (negative = up) used for jumps, falling objects and shadows; hit tests include a z half-depth. Each room has a bottom and a top collision layer, and entities carry a collision layer (1, 2 or 3 = both) switched by stairs/ladder/bridge tiles, giving multi-level rooms without 3D.

components.label: Centred follow camera clamped to room bounds with capped speed and screen shake
components.summary: Each frame the camera moves toward the target (normally Link) so that the target sits at screen (120, 80), with no dead zone, by at most scrollSpeed px per axis (4 by default; scripts and boss rooms set 1-2), and clamped to the room rectangle. Screen shake adds offsets up to +-3 px from a 6x8 table, advancing every 2 frames. Camera targets can be retargeted to objects (Minish form, cutscenes, world-event reveals).

components.label: Room-edge slide scrolling, door warps and typed fades
components.summary: Walking off a room edge either follows a border warp record or, within an area, slides the camera to the neighbour room at 4 px/frame (40 frames vertically, 60 horizontally) while nudging Link 0.375 or 0.25 px/frame so he ends inside. Doors, stairs and area rectangles use warp records (border, area-rect with 4 shapes, and variants) that pick a fade: default, black, white, mosaic cut or iris; durations are 256/speed frames (e.g. 16 frames at speed 16, 64 at speed 4). Spawn types include normal, drop-in, step-forward, stair exit and Minish variants.

components.label: Mode-0 tilemap rooms on two collision layers with OBJ actors
components.summary: Gameplay runs in Mode 0 with up to four text BGs: two map layers (LAYER_BOTTOM/LAYER_TOP) carry collision-bearing 16x16 metatiles, the others hold the HUD/text window and per-room decorative or parallax backdrops installed by background managers. Actors are OBJ sprites (up to 62 visible in the frontend capture). Map edits at runtime (kinstone world events, bombed walls, opened chests) rewrite tile types in place.

components.label: HBlank-DMA window and affine raster effects (iris wipes, dark-room light circle, barrel, heat shimmer)
components.summary: A shared helper fills a per-scanline buffer and arms DMA0 (HBlank start, dest reload) to stream it into a register each line. Uses found: WIN0H per line for circular iris fades and the Minish-portal close-up, and a light circle centred on Link in dark rooms (radius eased in 4 px steps with a sine wobble); BG2PA..BG2PD-style affine parameters per line for the Deepwood Shrine rolling-barrel interior; BG3HOFS per line for steam overlays, light rays and Vaati's appearing effect; BG3CNT per line in one pause screen; a rotating white-triangle polygon window. The captured front end did not exercise any of them (no HBlank DMA recorded).

components.label: Mode-1 affine title zoom and affine BG set pieces
components.summary: The title switches to Mode 1 and draws the Picori sword on affine BG2 (256-colour, 512x256 wrap) with BLDALPHA 9/9 between BG0 and BG1; the sword zooms out from a scale ratio of 0x10 to 0x100 in 0x10 steps (15 frames) via BgAffineSet, centred at (120, 72). In play, affine hardware appears in set pieces (rolling barrel) rather than routine actors; no affine OBJs were seen in the captured front end.

components.label: Alpha overlays, light levels and screen fades
components.summary: Outdoor and dungeon atmospherics are layered BGs with alpha blending (Hyrule Field cloud shadows, Cave of Flames steam, Mount Crenel weather), room light levels lerped toward a target in steps of 4 (of 256), and a fade controller offering black/white fades and iris wipes. The intro story uses alpha blending plus WIN0 to frame stained-glass panels.

components.label: Scale-selling parallax on Minish paths and rafters
components.summary: When Link is Minish-sized on dedicated "Minish path" rooms, background managers rebuild BG1/BG3 from wide source maps and scroll them at more than camera speed horizontally (BG3 at 1.125x, BG1 at 1.25x) and at a damped ratio vertically (BG3 at 0.25x around a 48 px anchor), so giant grass blades and clutter sweep past as if close to the lens. Minish rafters use per-layer ratio tables relative to room width/height.

components.label: MP2K (m4a) sequencer at 15768 Hz with a fade-aware request wrapper
components.summary: Audio is Nintendo's m4a/MP2K library: m4aSoundInit sets 8-bit DAC, 15768 Hz mix, 8 DirectSound channels, master volume 15; the mixer runs from a VCOUNT interrupt at line 80 (the handler is named HBlankIntr) and VSync from VBlank. Game code goes through SoundReq, which encodes commands in the high half-word (stop, fade in/out, tempo, continue) and keeps separate master/BGM/SFX volumes that fade 4/256 per frame. Capture confirms DirectSound A only at 15768 Hz plus PSG channels 1, 2 and 4.

components.label: Area-keyed BGM with fight-theme overrides
components.summary: Each area's metadata names a queued BGM; on room load the game only restarts music when the queued track differs from the playing one. Fight managers swap in a room-specified or default fight theme and restore the previous track when the fight is cleared; a late-game story flag forces the fight theme area-wide; boss deaths stop the BGM. About 100 BGM ids exist in the sound table.

components.label: Instant-start 8-direction walk with normalised diagonals and state speed table
components.summary: The D-pad maps to 8 of 32 directions (opposite pairs cancel). Walking has no acceleration: each frame PlayerNormal writes speed directly (1.25 px/frame) and the move is speed x sin/cos of the direction, so diagonals have the same magnitude (0.707 per axis). Facing keeps the current cardinal when it is adjacent to a diagonal input. A per-frame speed modifier (slopes, dust, swamp, beetles) is added then reset, with a 0.125 px/frame floor. State-specific speeds replace the base: shield/bow 0.75, sword charge 0.875, Gust Jar 0.5, burning forced run 3.0, Minish 0.75.

components.label: Quarter-tile collision masks, axis wall-sliding and corner nudge
components.summary: Each 16x16 tile per layer has a collision byte: values 1-15 are a 4-bit mask of solid 8x8 quarters, larger values select 16x16 per-pixel shape masks (diagonals, half tiles). The player samples 8 probe points around a 12x12 hitbox and writes per-side collision bits; a per-direction mask cancels only the blocked axis, so diagonal input slides along walls. Walking straight into a wall edge where only one leading probe is blocked redirects the move 90 degrees toward the open side at 1 px/frame (corner nudge), and cardinal input into a diagonal shape tile rotates the heading 45 degrees. After moving, edge points are pushed pixel by pixel out of shape masks. The shape-mask table is chosen by state (normal, Minish, jumping, carrying, beetle, swimming), which is how small gaps open only to Minish…

components.label: Per-tile surface actions (ice momentum, conveyors, swamp, slopes)
components.summary: Every frame the act tile under Link maps to one of 46 surface types with its own handler. Ice switches to velocity physics: +-10/256 px/frame^2 per axis toward input (diagonals unnormalised), -3/256 friction, +-1.5 px/frame cap, and normal-ground movement seeds the velocity so momentum carries onto ice. Conveyors push at 1.25 px/frame (not Minish). Swamp slows and sinks Link over up to 240 frames before a 4-unit penalty respawn (dashing is immune). Slopes, dust and attached beetles subtract speed.

components.label: R-button roll and Pegasus Boots charge-dash
components.summary: Roll (R with a direction) runs a 4-step speed script by animation frame (2.0, +0.125, 3.0, 0 px/frame); big Link is briefly harmless to enemies during it, and on ice it rolls in place. Pegasus Boots charge for ~30 frames (walking blocked), then dash at 3.0 px/frame (2.5 as Minish), steering 11.25 degrees per frame toward held input; two consecutive full wall contacts make Link bounce back (1 px/frame, z velocity 2.0, screen shake 16). With the Dash Attack skill and a sword the dash carries a sword hitbox. Dashing also crosses swamp safely.

components.label: Roc's Cape z-jump with held glide extension
components.summary: Top-down jumping is purely on the z axis: the Cape sets z velocity 2.0 px/frame with gravity 0.125 px/frame^2 (doubled over layer-transition tiles), clearing pits and low obstacles for ~33 frames and ~17 px of height. Holding the button at the apex re-launches at 2.0 with gravity halved to 0.0625 (a glide). Air control becomes velocity-based: 1 px/frame initial in the input direction, +-3/256 per frame within 90 degrees of facing, 6/256 against, capped at 1.5 px/frame with no air friction. Only swords can be used airborne; Down Thrust (skill) adds a 2.5 boost then double gravity.

components.label: Ledge hops, push/pull, ladders, holes and swimming
components.summary: Pushing against a ledge for 6 frames hops down with z velocity scaled to the drop ((16n-4)/16 px/frame for n tiles) at 1 px/frame forward, invulnerable mid-air. Pushing a block for 6 frames starts a scripted push at 0.5 px/frame (0.25 Minish); pulling moves 0.5 px/frame backward. Ladders force both layers and climb at an animation-driven speed; climbable walls need the Grip Ring. Big Link can drop into holes and hop out by holding a direction for 8 frames. With Flippers Link swims at 0.75 (1.0 with the swim butterfly) with an A burst to 1.5 decaying 4/256 per frame, and can dive for 120 frames; without them deep water drowns.

components.label: Matrix-driven knockback slide and signed i-frame counters
components.summary: Contact outcomes (damage, knockback speed and duration, i-frames, confusion) come from a 173x34 collision matrix indexed by attacker hit type and victim hurt type. Knocked-back Link slides at a fixed 2.5 px/frame through the wall-aware mover until the duration expires (cancelled while dashing, holding, jumping, swimming, falling or rolling). I-frames are a signed counter ticking toward zero; pairs with non-zero i-frames skip collision. A front shield block gives 128 frames of contact immunity.

components.label: Pit, water, lava and swamp hazards with breadcrumb respawn
components.summary: Falling into a pit costs 2 units (1/4 heart) with 32 i-frames; lava 2 units after a bounce; swamp 4 units; damaging floors 2 units with knockback; drowning costs no health. After a hazard Link respawns on the most recent safe tile from a 16-entry breadcrumb list of ground tiles recorded at z == 0 (or on the lily pad he rode, or the room entry point). Some pits are exits that drop Link into the room below without damage.

components.label: Portal-based shrinking to Minish scale with scale-specific rules
components.summary: Link shrinks only on Minish portals (stumps, pots, etc.): a manager tracks a 64x64 px area around each portal; Link jumps onto it (z velocity 2.0, approach 1 px/frame), presses R to activate, and an affine-scaled shrink animation sets PL_MINISH (some scripted rays also shrink him). Ezlo must have joined first. Growing back requires standing on a portal again (scale 1152 -> 256 in steps of 32). As Minish Link: hitbox 4x4 (vs 12x12), walk 0.75, dash 2.5, push 0.25 px/frame; only swords (no spin/charge), orbs and pick-up are usable (no bombs, bow, boomerang, shield, Gust Jar, cane, mitts, cape, boots, ocarina, bottles); he cannot lift objects or use small/big keys; puddles drown him and holes act as pits; conveyors ignore him; separate collision-shape tables open Minish-only cracks and Minis…

components.label: Two-button item loadout with a Zelda tool set
components.summary: Two equip slots (A and B) hold any of the activatable items; a new item auto-equips to an empty slot or replaces the item of the same menu category; R is a context action (roll, shrink/grow, talk). Tools: swords (5 tiers), bombs (3 at once, 150-frame fuse) and remote bombs, bow and light arrows, boomerang and magic boomerang, shield and mirror shield, lantern, Gust Jar (suction and blow), Cane of Pacci (flip objects/enemies, launch from holes), Mole Mitts (dig), Roc's Cape, Pegasus Boots, Ocarina of Wind and four bottles. Each item has a Minish-usability bit and a priority; airborne Link may only use swords.

components.label: Sword swings, charge spin and learnable techniques
components.summary: Swinging spawns a sword hitbox whose hurt type depends on sword tier and move (swing, spin, roll thrust, charge, down thrust); actual damage comes from the collision matrix. Holding the button charges a spin attack in 80 frames (40 with Fast Spin). Eight scroll techniques are learned from the Blade Brothers and each is a skill bit: Spin Attack, Rock Breaker, Dash Attack, Down Thrust, Roll Attack, Sword Beam (only at full health), Peril Beam (only at <= 1 heart), Great Spin (10 loops, 15 with Long Spin, spiral beam with the Four Sword); plus Fast Spin, Fast Split and Long Spin. Only one beam may exist at a time.

components.label: Four Sword clone splitting on clone tiles
components.summary: After a spin charge is held, standing on a special clone tile and continuing to hold builds a split charge (+6 per frame, +12 with Fast Split, to 800, about 134/67 frames, shown as a 40-segment bar); release spawns copies of Link that mirror his actions, used to push heavy blocks and press multiple switches. Clone count scales with sword tier (0/0/1/2/3 for Smith/Green/Red/Blue/Four Sword). Clones vanish when the charge drains or R is pressed.

evidence.ref: clones copy Link's movements and are used for multi-switch and heavy-block puzzles

components.label: Heart health in eighth units, charms and bottled restoratives
components.summary: Health is stored as 8 units per heart (start 24 = 3 hearts, max 160 = 20 hearts). Damage to Link is the attacker's damage value (from the collision matrix; hard-coded cases are 4 for fire, 2 for pits), quartered by Nayru's charm or halved by Farore's, minimum 1. Farore and Din charms multiply Link's outgoing damage by 1.5 and 2 for 3600 frames. Bottles hold potions (red: full, blue: 80 units), milk, fairies (32 units; a bottled fairy auto-revives at 0 health with 226 i-frames) and picolytes that bias drop tables for 900 frames.

components.label: Six-handler enemy FSM runtime with definition table and home box
components.summary: Every enemy kind is a function dispatched each frame through a six-entry handler table (OnTick, OnCollision, OnKnockback, OnDeath, OnConfused, OnGrabbed); OnTick indexes a per-species action array by the entity's action byte. A shared definition table gives per-form health, base speed, damage/hit type and collision mask. On init each enemy derives a home rectangle from per-species or room-supplied ranges (home = spawn - 4*range px, extent 8*range px); helpers test "inside home box" and "target inside home box" and steer back toward the box centre when outside. Death spawns a DEATH_FX object (which rolls the drop) and increments the save's enemies-killed counter; bosses flag themselves and stop the BGM instead.

components.label: Size-filtered enemy target selection (full-size vs Minish-scale threats)
components.summary: Enemies ask for a target through one of four selector functions. Selector 0 accepts the player unless busy/hidden/falling; selector 1 additionally ignores a Minish-sized player; selector 2 accepts the player only while Minish-sized; selector 3 ignores Minish, captured and item-disabled states. Almost every full-size species (Octorok, Darknut, Chuchu, Moblins, Wallmaster, Ghini, Gibdo, Puffstool) uses selector 1, so shrinking makes Link invisible to them, while Minish-scale critters (e.g. the aggressive cucco chick) use selector 2. The same world is therefore populated by two disjoint threat sets keyed on player scale.

components.label: Octorok-style pause/walk/turn wanderer that spits when facing the player
components.summary: Octoroks alternate a pause (24-80 frames) and a walk of 30/60/60/90 frames in one of four cardinal directions. Turning picks a random cardinal while inside the home box, otherwise heads back toward home (with a +-45 degree jitter 3 times in 4). The aggressive variant has a 1-in-4 chance to turn straight at the player when the player is in its home box; the stationary variant faces the player whenever possible. At the end of a walk, if its facing equals the rounded direction to the player, it spits a rock projectile (variant 0 needs a further 3-in-4 roll).

components.label: Rope-style axis-alignment charge
components.summary: Ropes wander inside their home box; once a 60-frame cooldown expires and the target is inside the box, an axis-alignment probe (12 px band, tile-checked line on the shared map layer) returns a cardinal direction and the rope charges along it at 1.625 px/frame (vs 0.5 base) for up to 30 frames. Hitting something resets the cooldown. Ropes can also drop from the ceiling (type 1) with a 24-unit gravity fall.

components.label: Chuchu proximity hop-attack and electrified/stateful variants
components.summary: Chuchus creep toward the target at 0.125 px/frame, re-aiming every 8 frames. When their timer runs out they hop at the player if within 56 px (horizontal speed 1.5 px/frame, z velocity 2 px/frame, gravity 0.25 px/frame^2), re-arm for 12-15 frames if within 72 px, otherwise sink and re-emerge elsewhere; standing in water also makes them submerge. Variants swap hit types to make the body temporarily unsafe (electrified) or armoured.

components.label: Keese random flutter with rest and proximity wake
components.summary: Keese fly in random 32-direction headings (re-chosen each flap animation, or toward home when outside the box) for a random flight budget, then rest 30-75 frames. If the player is more than 112 px away after a 60-frame grace period the keese sleeps and only wakes when the player comes within 112 px.

components.label: Darknut spacing, guard and counter-slash
components.summary: Darknuts close in on the target but, inside 56 px, back away if the path is clear (turning to face), keeping a fighting distance; inside 72 px with the target in front they pick an attack direction and spawn a sword-slash projectile. Their hit type flips between a guarded value and a vulnerable value around attacks, so frontal hits bounce except in post-attack windows; specific contact types (e.g. item stuns) knock them into a stunned state with star FX for a per-variant duration. Variants raise health (12/12/20/26).

components.label: Wallmaster ceiling drop and Like Like engulf/steal
components.summary: Two grab enemies. Wallmaster: when armed and a full-size target exists it teleports above the player at z=-128 px with a 90-frame shadow tell, falls 3 px/frame, closes its hand (grab hit type) and if it catches Link carries him up at 2 px/frame and transitions him out (back to the dungeon entrance); a miss re-arms after a per-instance delay x60 frames. Like Like: engulfs the player; each button press adds 1-2 to an escape counter (escape at 25); if a 95-frame timer runs out first it steals the Mirror Shield, else the Shield, else deals 1 unit of damage, and then releases. Release launches Link with z velocity 1.5 and 60 i-frames.

components.label: Spark wall-hugging circuit
components.summary: Sparks move along walls by turning on collision flags; the head variant turns one way and the tail variant the other, so they trace room obstacles clockwise or counter-clockwise. If no wall is felt for 120 frames they rotate 90 degrees to find one again. They are invulnerable (health 255).

components.label: Item-specific enemy reactions (Gust Jar suction, propeller removal, curl-up)
components.summary: OnCollision handlers branch on the attacker's contact type, giving each tool a distinct effect: Octoroks, Ropes and Keese have a Gust Jar "grabbed" handler with a suction tolerance timer after which they are pulled in and destroyed; Peahats lose their propeller to two specific contact types and become grounded and vulnerable; Rollobites curl up (invulnerable, pushable) and ride out knockback; Business Scrubs only become interactable after being stunned. This makes items act as typed keys against enemies, mirroring the lock-and-key world design.

components.label: Element-dungeon bosses with item-specific damage windows and phase health
components.summary: Bosses are multi-entity assemblies flagged EM_FLAG_BOSS whose health is often 255 (scripted) with damage routed through specific parts. Big Green Chuchu reacts to contact type 19 at its base (wobble counter, 180-frame window). Big Octorok cycles phases with health 3/1/3/1/3/1/3. Mazaal must be entered while Minish-sized: standing in a 3x3 px region at its head while PL_MINISH triggers a room transition into its body; its macro health crosses thresholds 60 and 30 that persist across those room changes. Gleerok, Gyorg pair and the Vaati forms reuse the multi-part pattern.

components.label: Monitored ambush fights that seal and resolve via flags
components.summary: A fight manager waits for an optional start flag, spawns the room's enemy list, tags each as monitored, switches to a fight BGM (room override or the default fight theme) and sets an Ezlo hint; when every monitored enemy is dead it sets a completion flag (used by doors/chests) and restores music. A completed fight never reloads.

components.label: Kinstone fusion - shape-matched halves shared with NPC fusers unlock remote world events
components.summary: The player collects kinstone halves (17 bag piece types: 9 gold, 3 red, 2 blue, 3 green shapes; up to 18 bag slots, 99 per type) and fuses them with "fusers" (NPCs, some enemies such as Business Scrubs, and objects). Each of 100 fusion ids has a colour, a shape and a world-event id; a fusion succeeds only when the piece the player offers has the same shape as the fuser's half. Success sets the fused bit, increments fusedCount (all 100 sets didAllFusions), then a world-event subtask loads the remote target room, scrolls the camera to the change for up to 300 frames and optionally drops a map marker. Effects are re-applied on every room load by checking the fused bit (chests appear, tiles are stamped, beanstalks and lily-pad rails spawn, golden enemies appear, etc.).

components.label: Business Scrub stun-then-trade shops
components.summary: Business Scrubs are hostile nut-shooters that become merchants after being stunned; each holds one offer from a table (the Bow as a special non-rupee offer, 30 arrows or 10 bombs for 30 rupees, Grip Ring for 40, a kinstone for 100 or 200, a bottle for 20) and some act as kinstone fusers. Purchase checks and deducts rupees.

components.label: Per-dungeon small keys, big key boss door, map and compass
components.summary: Each of seven dungeons has a small-key counter and an item bitfield (map 1, compass 2, big key 4) in the save. Small keys come from chests, ice blocks and drops; using one on a locked door or key block (via the interaction scan, never as Minish) decrements the counter and sets that door's flag so it stays open. The boss door only checks the big key (never consumed) and sets its own flag. Shutter doors open or close on flags (e.g. fight cleared) and can close behind the player. The map reveals floor layouts; the compass marks unopened chests and the uncleared boss room. Defeating a dungeon boss sets a global LVn_CLEAR flag and yields an element.

components.label: Tool-keyed obstacles and the dungeon-item loop
components.summary: Each dungeon awards a tool that is then the key for a family of world obstacles (bombable walls persisted by flags, destructible tiles, Gust Jar webs, Flipper water and lily pads, Grip Ring walls, lightable switches, ice blocks hiding keys, Minish cracks, clone-count switches), so the overworld is revisited as the toolkit grows. Room load callbacks re-apply world state from flags, inventory and wind crests.

components.label: Banked persistent flags plus volatile room flags and enemy memory
components.summary: Flags are encoded with a 2-bit scope (local bank of the current area, global, room) and a 10-bit index. Persistent flags live in 512 bytes (4096 bits) split into a global bank and 13 local banks assigned per area (overworld, town, caves, each dungeon). Room flags (416 bits) are cleared on every room load. A separate 8-room MRU memory keeps up to 32 killed-enemy bits per room so recently cleared rooms stay cleared; it is wiped on game start, so enemies respawn when you travel far enough.

components.label: Global progress level and story flags
components.summary: A single global_progress value (1-9) is recomputed from milestone flags (dungeon clears, Vaati's takeover, meeting King Gustaf, the stained-glass event). It gates which fusers offer kinstones, figurine availability, hint tables and NPC states. Other one-time story flags (meeting Ezlo, leaving on the quest) gate portals and enemy population (the main enemy lists load only after the quest starts).

components.label: Hub overworld of linked areas with layered dungeons and Minish sub-world
components.summary: The world is a set of areas (up to 64 rooms each) around Hyrule Town - Minish Woods, Hyrule Field, Castor Wilds, Mt Crenel, Veil Falls, Lake Hylia, Cloud Tops, Royal Valley and others - with element dungeons opening off them. A Minish-scale layer of interiors and paths (Minish Village, Minish paths, rafters, holes in walls) overlays the same places and is entered through portals. Areas are tagged overworld/dungeon/has-keys/has-map, and first visits show an area-name banner.

components.label: Ezlo hints, map markers and region-triggered advice
components.summary: Ezlo (the talking cap) gives context hints two ways. Region managers freeze Link for 30 frames and show a one-shot hint when he enters a rectangle. Pressing Select picks the latest satisfied milestone from a progression table (43 milestones checked by item owned, kinstone fused or flag) and cycles through 8 hint texts, reshuffling after 8 without immediate repeats. Fusions with a marker icon and map-hint subtasks place markers on the map.

components.label: Wind crest activation and Ocarina fast travel
components.summary: Eight wind crests (Mt Crenel, Veil Falls, Cloud Tops, Hyrule Town, Lake Hylia, Castor Wilds, South Hyrule Field, Minish Woods) are stored in the top 8 bits of a save word and lit by touching them. After obtaining the Ocarina of Wind, a fast-travel subtask cycles through lit crests only and warps there; warping is allowed only in overworld areas flagged for it.

components.label: Sword techniques bought from dojo masters
components.summary: Sword techniques are inventory items (one skill bit each) taught by the Blade Brothers in a fixed order (Spin, Rock Breaker, Dash, Down Thrust, Roll, Sword Beam, Peril Beam, Great Spin, then Fast Spin, Fast Split, Long Spin); the pause menu lists 8 technique slots. Skills are recomputed from inventory every frame they matter.

components.label: Rupees, ammo and shells with upgradeable capacities
components.summary: Rupees (values 1/5/20/50/100/200) are capped by a 4-tier wallet (100/300/500/999); bombs by a 4-tier bomb bag (10/30/50/99) and arrows by a 4-tier quiver (30/50/70/99), each upgrade refilling the pool. Mysterious Shells cap at 999. Heart pieces (4 = +1 heart) and containers raise max health and fully heal. HUD counters tick toward the true value one unit per frame and turn yellow at a full wallet.

components.label: Weighted 16-slot drop tables with need-aware boosts and picolyte bias
components.summary: Drops sum a source table (per-enemy, per-area, per-object) with modifiers into 16 integer weights (none, rupees, hearts, fairy, bombs, arrows, shells, three kinstone colours, beetle) and roll Random() % sum from a random start slot. Need-aware boosts add +5 hearts at <= 1 heart, +3 bombs or +3 arrows when empty, +1 five-rupee at <= 10 rupees; modifiers of -999 remove shells after all figurines and kinstones after all fusions. A rolled item the player cannot use (bombs without a bag, arrows without a bow, shells before the Earth Element, kinstones without the bag) becomes nothing. Picolyte bottles add large weights to one category for 900 frames.

components.label: Fixed-price shops for gear, ammo, food and bottle contents
components.summary: Stockwell's shop, the bakery and other merchants sell from a price table (purchase requires price <= rupees, then deducts). Representative prices are in the table; capacity upgrades (bomb bag, quiver) are the big rupee sinks.

components.label: Mysterious Shell figurine gacha with pity floor
components.summary: Shells buy draws at a figurine machine. The chance of a new figurine is 100 x (available - owned) / available percent, +1 % per extra shell inserted, with a floor that drops as the collection grows (15 % under 50 owned, 12 % under 80, 9 % under 110, else 6 %). A miss returns a duplicate. Availability widens with story progress (136 figurines; 130 before the credits). Completing the set grants the Carlov Medal and removes shells from drop tables.

components.label: Hearts, rupee, key counter and A/B/R button HUD
components.summary: The HUD shows up to 20 hearts in two rows of 10 with quarter-heart resolution (health catches up 1 quarter every 2 frames on gain), a 3-digit rupee counter, a dungeon key counter only in key areas, A and B item icons with ammo counts, an R label naming the context action (e.g. Shrink/Grow at a portal), and a 40-segment charge bar for sword split charging. Buttons slide away while messages are shown. A low-health beep plays every 90 frames below the threshold.

components.label: Multi-screen pause menu (items, quest status, maps, kinstones, techniques, save/sleep)
components.summary: Start opens a set of screens switched with L/R - item grid (equip to A/B), quest status (kinstone bag tier, heart pieces, techniques count, shells), overworld map or dungeon map (with map/compass data), kinstone piece list, sword techniques, and save and sleep prompts. Screens cross-fade by alpha 2 per frame; the overworld map is skipped until the map item is owned.

components.label: Script-bytecode cutscenes and typewriter dialogue boxes
components.summary: NPCs, cutscenes and world events run a u16 script bytecode (139 commands - flag ops, waits, fades, movement, messages, item/rupee/health grants, camera target and scroll speed). Messages print in a 26x4-tile window (two 208 px lines per page) at 5/3/1 frames per character, 8x faster while B is held, with up to 4 choices; the box jumps to the top if the speaker is low on screen. Ezlo comments constantly as a companion voice.

components.label: Stained-glass story intro and staff roll
components.summary: New games open with a narrated stained-glass slideshow (Picori legend) framed by a window and alpha blending, then a playable prologue from Link's bedroom. Completing the game plays the staff roll, records saw_staffroll and the GAMECLEAR flag (unlocking the last figurines) and prompts to save.

components.label: Hyrule seen from two scales - Picori folklore fantasy
components.summary: High-fantasy Hyrule where the tiny Picori (Minish) secretly live alongside humans; the sorcerer Vaati petrifies Princess Zelda, and Link, guided by Ezlo (a talking cap who can shrink him), restores the Picori Blade with four elements. Bright, whimsical tone; much of the charm comes from seeing ordinary places at Minish scale.

games.name: Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga

components.label: Priority-ordered engine process scheduling
components.summary: Implementation component, not a combat rule: process_add inserts a process in an ascending-priority linked list, placing it after existing equal priorities. process_execute_all calls enabled nonwaiting process callbacks and increments their local update counter; repeated execution and signed executeMax branches exist, but their gameplay use is unknown.

components.label: Selective process suspension
components.summary: process_disable_all suspends processes except priorities 0 and 255. process_enable_all enables every listed process and marks each waiting, allowing engine service callbacks to remain distinct from paused activity; which gameplay systems use the protected priorities is not established.

components.label: Process removal repairs active iteration links
components.summary: process_remove repairs neighboring linked-list pointers and adjusts currentProcess or nextProcess when the removed object is being visited. Storage is freed only when the FREE flag is set; this is a lifecycle primitive rather than proof of a save or gameplay rollback mechanism.

components.label: Stateful publisher-logo presentation
components.summary: comp_init constructs Mario, Luigi and AlphaDream logo sprites and a drawing subprocess. comp_update advances an authored fall, shake, hold and brightness sequence before creating the title process; A/B/START are tested in the AlphaDream presentation states rather than universally in every logo state.

components.label: Logo-phase peripheral signal detection
components.summary: gbpl_update reads active-low D-pad hardware, computes newly asserted directions and detects a narrow all-directions timing pattern during the logo process. Two qualifying events with a nonzero previous timestamp and spacing under four process-counter ticks set a capability flag later used by the rumble option; physical Game Boy Player compatibility was not tested.

components.label: Suitcase-based title-state machine
components.summary: The recovered title has fade-in, title-animation, press-start-show, press-start-wait, suitcase-opens, game-select and fade-out states. Individual suitcase and logo items advance their own substates, keeping presentation completion distinct from accepting a menu choice.

components.label: Conditioned title-animation skip
components.summary: During title animation, A/B/SELECT/START trigger skipping only when skipSuitcaseAnim is true and a skip is not already underway. The transition fades, reconstructs the title state and resumes through fade-in; this is not evidence that all story scenes can be skipped.

components.label: Title waits for A or START
components.summary: The title visibly presents a start prompt. In its press-start-wait state, A or START starts a suitcase/menu transition and queues sound effect 96; unrelated input does not take this branch.

components.label: Cyclic three-entry game selector
components.summary: The recovered menu distinguishes Mario & Luigi, Mario Bros. and options. UP/DOWN wrap the selected index across 0..2, while A/START has priority over navigation in the same update; the bean pointer moves to y=92+20*selection.

components.label: Fade-boundary dispatch to game, bundled mode or options
components.summary: After a 16-count fade-out, the selected route creates the LOAD process for Mario & Luigi, calls the bundled Mario Bros. entry, or creates OPTN. The title removes its drawing process, stops DMA0 and releases its own process before dispatch; downstream game-load/save semantics remain unknown.

components.label: Options interaction is gated during modal animation
components.summary: optn_update refuses normal selection processing while the window animates, while a cooldown is active, or when A is asserted in that state. Otherwise UP/DOWN wrap across three rows and B attempts persistence; the source exposes different input fields for navigation and direct actions without fully recovering their repeat semantics.

components.label: Three persistent feature-option bits
components.summary: The recovered option definitions label bits as easy sleep, rumble and auto feature. Directional input changes staged bits; rumble is editable only when the peripheral flag equals one. The actual sleep trigger and timeout behavior is not recovered, so these labels establish stored configuration rather than implementation of sleeping.

components.label: Feature-enable confirmation and animated return
components.summary: Enabling each labeled feature enters its own confirmation state. A acknowledges only after the window animation reaches zero; rumble acknowledgment additionally sets the runtime flag and a 16-update cooldown. This establishes acknowledgement ordering, not the human meaning of every confirmation text.

components.label: Staged option persistence with explicit return value
components.summary: try_save_options copies staged bits into runtime fields and an EEPROM-related structure before invoking sub_812454C. On B in the selection state, its boolean result chooses leave or save-error state. No power-loss atomicity, record checksum or complete save format is established by the recovered wrapper.

components.label: Failed settings save receives a separate acknowledgement state
components.summary: A failed option-write result enters a save-error state rather than the success transition. After modal opening finishes, the error screen leaves after 240 countdown updates or A/B/START; this is a settings error path and does not establish safe campaign-save recovery.

components.label: Presentation-only fixed-point falling and rebound
components.summary: comp_update applies explicit velocity and acceleration to the startup Mario/Luigi sprites and background offset, with a fixed rebound velocity after the landing threshold. Sprite coordinates are rendered by division by 256. These are authored logo-animation dynamics, not playable-character gravity, jump strength or collision behavior.

components.label: Measured tile-mode presentation and scenes
components.summary: The retained three-phase run records display modes 0 and 1, layered backgrounds and OBJ sprites. No bitmap-mode usage was observed in this run, which does not exclude bitmap techniques elsewhere in the game.

components.label: Title lettering uses an affine background transform
components.summary: open_update builds a BG affine matrix for the title lettering and writes BG2 transform registers. The no-input attract phase records 55 frames with a transformed affine background, while later phases contain affine-capable layers without the same transformed-frame signal.

components.label: Affine sprites are present in the measured front end
components.summary: The title code animates logo sprite scales and the harness records affine OBJ use, with a peak count of six. This is an observed presentation technique rather than proof that battle sprites use affine transforms.

components.label: HBlank DMA0 drives per-line background scrolling
components.summary: sub_8056224 constructs a scanline-value table and configures DMA0 to the BG1 horizontal-scroll register at 0x04000014. Attract telemetry records this destination and 3181 frames with at least 32 rewritten visible lines, giving a source-plus-measurement link for the front-end effect.

components.label: HBlank window-shape transitions
components.summary: The frontend phase records HBlank DMA3 transfers to 0x04000040 using 32-bit width and one-unit count, with alternating source tables. A directly inspected keyframe shows a circular reveal. The transfer evidence supports a window-boundary effect but the exact geometric table generator has not been recovered.

components.label: State transitions use hardware brightness coefficients
components.summary: Title and options transitions update buffered BLDY while switching states. The observed run records brighten effects; frontend counters typically traverse 16 brightness steps, but their duration in hardware frames has not been independently aligned to the callback cadence.

components.label: Alpha blending is observed during entered scenes
components.summary: The frontend and gameplay-named cold-boot phases record 1025 and 1021 frames respectively in alpha-blend configuration. The exact actors or surfaces affected are not identified; this component records the hardware capability used in those scenes.

components.label: EWRAM shadow registers separate state updates from hardware access
components.summary: buffer_io_reg.h defines register shadows at 0x02000000 plus hardware register offsets, and the recovered frontend functions update these aliases. This is an engine boundary useful for tracing presentation state; the complete flush routine and its scheduling are not established here.

components.label: Explicit frontend resource uploads and temporary buffers
components.summary: comp_init obtains temporary RAM, invokes an opaque data-expansion callback, then CpuFastSet uploads character data and maps to selected BG VRAM regions. It also creates named sprite resources. Compression format, file-to-ROM resource mapping and asset reuse compatibility are not inferred from these calls.

components.label: Measured DirectSound and PSG coexistence
components.summary: The retained run reports active DirectSound A and B, the timer-derived FIFO rate 15768 Hz, and triggers on PSG channels 1 through 4. These are emulator hardware observations; the WAV output is resampled to 16 kHz mono and must not be confused with the native FIFO rate or a complete instrument inventory.

components.label: Distinct navigation and confirmation sound events
components.summary: The recovered title and options handlers call sound effect 95 for row changes and 96 for confirmation. This establishes event-to-resource dispatch without identifying the waveform, composition or audio-engine family.

components.label: Oblique room art with visible floor depth
components.summary: Inspected opening-room frames show a floor plane, upright characters and architectural surfaces with vertical depth cues. This supports a three-quarter visual projection; it does not establish coordinate axes, collision shapes, stair traversal or a 3D simulation.

components.label: Authored opening-room staging
components.summary: The new capture moves from a masked transition into a furnished room with characters, stairs and a doorway. Different inspected frames show a character at different room positions, but no counterfactual input replay was performed, so whether this is directly player-controlled motion or scripted movement remains unresolved.

components.label: Bright outlined pixel-art interiors
components.summary: The inspected room uses saturated yellows and pinks, outlined small characters, patterned floors and decorative furnishings. This is a local visual-style observation, not an assessment of the complete setting, plot or asset licensing.

components.label: Menu choice previews transition through disappear and appear states
components.summary: Changing selection starts disappearance of the suitcase preview. Once the preview animation completion flag is set, the handler selects the next preview animation and returns it to idle; menu preview state and selected route are distinct.

components.label: Inferred strategy: choose the shorter cyclic menu route
components.summary: Inference from the source only: with three cyclic entries and an observed current selection, a user can reach either other entry with one appropriately directed UP or DOWN action. This is a menu-navigation affordance, not a measured combat or exploration strategy and not evidence that the capture executed this policy.

evidence.ref: Choose shorter direction on the recovered three-entry cycle.

components.label: Inferred skill: recognize when the front end accepts input
components.summary: Inference from explicit input gates: a user can wait for the correct title or confirmation state before sending a selection action, reducing the chance an action is ignored by an animation gate. No user study or timing-reliability experiment was performed; this is an inferred interaction skill, with unknown gameplay transfer.

evidence.ref: Combine title skip/start gates with options animation gates.

components.label: Scene callback lifecycle
components.summary: Startup initializes graphics, input, audio, interrupts and save handling before selecting title_main. Each scene main callback controls whether the loop continues; scene completion resets the scanline scheduler and DMA queue before the next frame-processing transition.

components.label: Title-to-menu transition
components.summary: A or Start advances selected title phases, including an early phase that waits until its counter exceeds thirty-two. Transition state twenty-two brightens the screen across ten updates before arranging the main menu; exact title phase timing depends on music-state signals.

components.label: Clamped main and link submenu selection
components.summary: The main menu has three entries and the link submenu has two. Up/down repeats clamp selection to valid bounds; A/Start accepts an enabled item and B restores the parent cursor from the link submenu.

components.label: Save flags select title appearance
components.summary: Title initialization begins with sunset and night flags true, then clears each when any corresponding entry in a saved five-by-three matrix is nonzero. This proves save-conditioned presentation; the meaning of those opaque matrix fields and their gameplay completion requirements have not been established.

components.label: Input edges and held-mask repetition
components.summary: Each of four input slots converts active-low button bits into held and newly triggered masks. An unchanged held mask repeats after a default twenty-four updates and then every six; changing or releasing the held mask resets the delay.

components.label: Bounded active/passive actor contact lists
components.summary: Active actors are tested against active and passive actors, while passive/passive pairs are absent. Insertion returns false once the active or passive capacity is reached, exposing a concrete resource limit rather than an inferred enemy count.

components.label: Cyclic checkpoint neighborhood collision filtering
components.summary: The normal path sorts both collision lists by checkpoint and checks a window from checkpoint minus two to checkpoint plus three with wraparound. Actors with checkpoint ID 127 are skipped by the fast path; a mode-bit branch instead uses all active/active and active/passive pairs, so checkpoint locality is an assumption of the optimization rather than a universal physical rule.

components.label: Three-coordinate overlap dispatches both actor callbacks
components.summary: Collision first rejects self-pairs and compares absolute X/Y/Z separation against summed per-axis sizes shifted left by fourteen. Surviving pairs invoke both nonnull callbacks only when the bitwise OR of their field_38 values is at most one; physical responses and item effects live in the callbacks and remain unextracted.

components.label: Lap, position, timer and course map
components.summary: The directly viewed race image shows LAP 1/3, eighth position, five coins, a timer, racer-order portraits, an empty item box and a small course map. These are observed display elements; lap advancement, coin handling, item distribution and ranking algorithms have not yet been read.

components.label: Continue, try again and quit over race scene
components.summary: The directly viewed overlay offers Continue, Try Again and Quit while preserving the race image behind it. Input behavior, whether race simulation is paused and the exact restart/reset scope require tracing before operational rules are assigned.

components.label: Behind-kart road-plane presentation
components.summary: The directly viewed race image presents a kart from behind with a road narrowing toward the horizon and billboard-like opponents and scenery. Combined with the affine scanline capture, this supports a pseudo-3D presentation interpretation, but not a recovered camera projection matrix.

components.label: Per-line affine background DMA in captured racing session
components.summary: The capture records DMA0 targeting address 0x04000020 in the affine-background register group, with at least thirty-two affected scanlines in 4090 frames. This is evidence of per-line affine rendering during the recorded session; correlating exact coefficients and individual race frames remains necessary before claiming a recovered road projection model.

components.label: Ordered scanline interrupt callbacks
components.summary: Callbacks are inserted in scanline order, and the compare register is set to the first callback scanline. The interrupt handler executes the current callback and advances or wraps to the next entry; title code uses a callback to change WINOUT at a particular scanline.

components.label: VBlank coordinates DMA, sprites, palettes and maps
components.summary: The VBlank handler stops DMA0, transfers buffered OAM, processes the queued DMA3 requests and uploads dirty palette and map buffers. The scene callback then writes scene-specific registers before link processing and the frame-complete flag; this establishes a concrete display lifecycle.

components.label: Deferred graphics copies split into 2048-byte DMA chunks
components.summary: Queued transfer entries retain source, destination and hardware configuration. Processing splits each entry into chunks of at most 2048 bytes, applies increment/decrement addressing modes and resets the queue heap after completion.

components.label: Two dirty tilemap buffers
components.summary: Two 1024-entry maps expose 32-wide coordinate indexing. A bitmask marks changed buffers and each selected map is copied to its configured hardware destination before the dirty bit is cleared.

components.label: Buffered palette upload
components.summary: Palette storage consists of two 256-color banks and a shared dirty flag. When dirty, the buffer is copied to palette RAM and the flag is cleared, otherwise the upload is skipped.

components.label: Thirty-two buffered sprite transform slots
components.summary: The affine helper writes four coefficients into the OAM transform layout and returns an incrementing slot index. It rejects allocation after slot thirty-one, while capture telemetry independently observed twenty-six affine sprites at peak.

components.label: Scale selects one of four sprite detail levels
components.summary: A scale input chooses level zero through three and the selected level shift adjusts the scale passed to the common cell renderer. The thresholds are native scale values; their relation to scene distance and game-world size was not recovered.

components.label: Mode zero and affine mode one across capture
components.summary: The retained capture reports 3880 mode-zero frames and 4988 mode-one frames from a 9000-frame request. Because those counts sum to 8868, 132 requested frames are not represented in the mode histogram; no rendering mode is invented for the missing observations.

components.label: Captured DirectSound A plus four PSG channels
components.summary: The capture recorded DirectSound A on 8996 frames and no DirectSound B frames, with a predominant timer-derived 10512 Hz rate. All four PSG channels were triggered; these are bounded observations and do not establish the full soundtrack instrumentation.

components.label: Separate move, accept, reject and cancel sounds
components.summary: Title navigation plays one song ID on cursor change, separate IDs on accepted or disabled selections, and a distinct cancel ID when leaving the link submenu. The source therefore distinguishes these interface events audibly without needing to infer which musical timbres the samples contain.

components.label: Bright castle-bordered track
components.summary: The directly viewed race shows a bounded gray circuit, grassy margins, checkered start markings, rounded trees and a large colorful castle. This is a visual motif record for one course, not a characterization of every circuit or the broader fiction.

components.label: Three fixed-stride records enter state1
components.summary: Instruction-verified helper zeroes words at 0x03001740 and 0x02000000, stores its argument at 0x03001744, then sets three state bytes at 0x03001748+i*24 to 1. The three records are an observed initialization span; allocation capacity and whether they are tasks, channels or actors remain unknown.

components.label: Indexed record gets state2 and a work-buffer address
components.summary: For raw index i, the helper addresses a24-byte record at 0x03001748+i*24, stores the second argument at+4 and a work-buffer address 0x03000b20+i*1536 at+8, clears+1 and+2, then writes state 2 at+0. There is no local index check; pairing it with the three-record initializer requires caller enforcement of 0<=i<3, which is not proven here.

components.label: Conditional pool-node transfer with16-bit count decrement
components.summary: The helper loads pool+0x10 as a candidate node. If nonzero, it pops the next pointer from node+0, decrements pool+0x0a as a16-bit quantity, rewires node links and pool+0x18 through an existing writable link, and clears node+0x0a,+0x0c,+0x10; otherwise it returns zero without these writes. This resembles pool allocation, but node role and pool invariants are not supplied by names.

components.label: Prepend one node through an indexed head slot
components.summary: Instructions multiply the raw index by 4, read the selected head word, store that prior value in the first word of the supplied node and then replace the head with the node pointer. No traversal, allocation or bounds checking occurs; the surrounding indexing meaning remains unknown.

components.label: Cross-table key equality gates a16-bit value
components.summary: The helper truncates its input to 16 bits and selects an8-byte descriptor at 0x080d2c04. Its u16 selector at+4 indexes a12-byte table at 0x080d2b5c whose first word is a record pointer; the pointed record key must equal the descriptor key before the helper returns the halfword at record+4, otherwise it returns 0. The value is a halfword load, even though generated C misleadingly casts a word expression.

components.label: Commit three halfword shadows to blend registers
components.summary: Direct halfword loads/stores copy 0x02004f72 to 0x04000052,0x02004f74 to 0x04000054 and 0x02004f70 to 0x04000050, in that order. components.label: Write a pair of indexed halfword values
components.summary: The helper truncates index to 16 bits, scales by 2, then writes separate supplied halfwords at 0x03000210+2*i and 0x03000218+2*i. Neither index range nor bank extent is checked; the8-byte separation alone does not prove a four-entry array contract.

components.label: Clear one halfword and one word in differently strided banks
components.summary: For the low8 bits of the input, the helper clears a halfword at 0x03001ea8+i*32 and a word at 0x03001c58+i*4. It clears exactly these fields, not entire32-byte records; the fields may belong to a shared slot system, but their gameplay role is unknown.

components.label: Read one bit from an indexed packed halfword
components.summary: Instructions truncate index and bit-offset inputs to 16 bits, load a halfword at base+2*(index>>3), then arithmetic-shift the zero-extended value by the low8 bits of 2*(index&7)+offset and mask bit0. Offset0 or 1 would select either bit of a two-bit cell, but the caller is not proven to restrict the offset to those values.

components.label: Set a bit in a16-bit-word bitset
components.summary: The low16 input bits choose word index i>>4 and bit i&15. A halfword load, OR and halfword store set the selected bit without clearing other bits; no index bounds or ownership checks are included.

components.label: Consume two bytes into an indirect context
components.summary: The helper reads an object-owned pointer at+0xcc, copies the next two stream bytes to context+2 and+3, and returns stream+2 in r0 before BX LR. This is a bounded stream-consumption primitive; the encoded command and field roles are unknown.

components.label: Project one raw state byte into two related fields
components.summary: After loading object+0xcc, the helper copies context+0x45 to+0x44 and uses that same u8 value to fetch a byte from ROM table 0x083ce09c into context+0x42. The ROM table extent and meaning of the three offsets are unresolved; names such as weapon, character or animation would be speculation.

components.label: Apply a ROM-selected three-word template
components.summary: A u8 selector indexes a ROM pointer table at 0x083ce0e4 with 4-byte entries. Three consecutive words from the selected target are copied into object+0x3c,+0x38,+0x40 in that order; these are raw parameters with unknown units and role, not established movement or weapon constants.
