games.name: Pokémon Emerald Version

components.label: Two-callback main loop with task scheduler and soft reset
components.summary: AgbMain reads keys, checks the soft-reset chord, then calls gMain.callback1 and callback2 each frame and waits for VBlank; every screen (copyright, title, menus, overworld, battle) is a callback2 with its own gMain.state machine, and cooperative work runs as up to 16 tasks. VBlank copies buffered GPU registers, services DMA3 requests, runs the m4a sound mixer and advances the RNG once. A VCount interrupt is armed at line 150. Key repeat starts after 40 frames and repeats every 5.

components.label: Copyright screen and three-scene skippable intro cinematic
components.summary: Boot shows a copyright screen (which also listens for a GameCube multiboot link for Colosseum/Box) and then the intro: scene 1 Game Freak logo over dripping leaves with a Flygon silhouette, scene 2 the player cycling with Torchic, Manectric, Volbeat and Flygon, scene 3 Groudon vs Kyogre ending with Rayquaza, then the title. Any new key press (once no palette fade is active) jumps to the title. In the capture the full cinematic runs ~3230 frames (~54 s) before the title appears.

components.label: Mode-1 title with affine logo, wavy clouds and intro loop
components.summary: Title setup fades from white, slides the Pokémon logo (256-colour affine BG2) up, shines it, alpha-fades in the EMERALD VERSION banner, then shows PRESS START over Rayquaza (BG0) and clouds (BG1) whose horizontal scroll is rippled per scanline by an HBlank-DMA sine wave. A/B/Start/Select skip each phase; A or Start opens the main menu. There is no gameplay demo: when the non-looping title BGM ends the game fades back to the copyright screen and replays the intro. Held combos open maintenance screens (B+Select+Up clear save, B+Select+Left reset RTC, B+Select berry-glitch fix).

components.label: Continue/New Game menu, professor introduction and character creation
components.summary: The main menu offers CONTINUE (if a valid save exists), NEW GAME, OPTION and, when unlocked, MYSTERY GIFT and MYSTERY EVENTS. New Game runs Professor Birch's speech on a spotlight platform with Lotad, a boy/girl choice, the naming keyboard and a yes/no confirmation, then shrinks the player sprite into the truck intro. The trainer ID is the value of hardware Timer 1, started when the naming screen opens and read when it closes. New saves start with 3000 money and the player in the moving truck.

components.label: Save-anywhere 128 KiB flash with rotating two-slot sector saves
components.summary: The player saves anywhere from the start menu. Flash is 32 sectors of 4 KiB: two 14-sector save slots (SaveBlock2, four SaveBlock1 sectors, nine PC-storage sectors) that alternate on each save, plus Hall of Fame (2), Trainer Hill and recorded-battle sectors. Each sector has a 3968-byte payload, a 16-bit folded checksum, a signature and a save counter; the slot with the higher valid counter loads. The sector order inside a slot rotates by one per save to spread flash wear, and the save blocks are relocated at a random RAM offset with a random encryption key for money/items (anti-memory-editing).

evidence.ref: pokeemerald:src/load_save.c (SaveBlock ASLR offset = (offset + Random()) & mask; encryptionKey from Random)

components.label: Whiteout to last heal point with half-money penalty
components.summary: When every party Pokémon faints (or the player loses a trainer battle) there is no game over screen: the whiteout script runs, money is halved, the party is fully healed and the player warps to the last Pokémon Center or home used as a heal location. Progress since the last save is kept because nothing is reloaded.

components.label: Mode-0 four-BG tile engine with text windows, 64-sprite OAM and palette fades
components.summary: Nearly everything renders in mode 0 with four text backgrounds managed through buffered BG templates, up to 32 text windows drawn into BG tilemaps, and a 64-slot sprite system with animation and affine command scripts that builds OAM each frame. A global palette-fade engine blends the buffered palettes toward a colour (typically black or white) and BLDY/BLDALPHA are used for screen and sprite fades. Battle animations and the intro lean on affine sprites (ObjAffineSet is the second most frequent BIOS call in the capture). Mode 1 is used only for affine title/intro layers and a few special screens.

evidence.ref: capture:attract+frontend video.mode_frames, blend_frames (alpha 4026, brighten 401, darken 155), obj_affine_frames 692

components.label: Three-layer 16x16 metatile map renderer with paired tilesets and animated tiles
components.summary: Maps are grids of u16 blocks: 10-bit metatile id, 2-bit collision and 4-bit elevation. Each metatile is eight 8x8 tiles (bottom and top 2x2 layers) plus an attribute word holding an 8-bit behaviour and a layer type that decides which of BG1 (above sprites), BG2 and BG3 receive the layers: NORMAL draws bottom to BG2 and top to BG1 so treetops and roofs cover the player; COVERED draws to BG3/BG2 (both under sprites); SPLIT uses BG3 and BG1. A layout pairs a primary tileset (shared, 512 tiles/metatiles, 6 palettes) with a secondary per-town tileset (512 more, 7 palettes); tileset callbacks DMA new tile graphics on a 16-frame cycle to animate water, flowers and waterfalls. Outside the layout, border metatiles repeat; connected maps are stitched in at edges.

evidence.ref: pokeemerald:include/global.fieldmap.h:struct MapLayout, struct Tileset, struct MapHeader, struct MapConnection

components.label: Map weather with particle sprites, palette colour maps and blend layers
components.summary: Each map header names a weather; coordinate events can change it. Weather is a callback set (init, main, finish) per type: rain/thunderstorm/downpour spawn rain sprites and darken palettes via colour-map index 3 (thunder adds flashes), snow and volcanic ash spawn particles, fog and sandstorm draw a semi-transparent BG/sprite layer, shade darkens, drought brightens with a pulsing BLDY lighten and dedicated colour tables, underwater bubbles rise. Route 119/123 cycle weathers and the "abnormal" weather alternates rain and drought during the Groudon/Kyogre crisis. Rain/sandstorm/drought carry into battle as battle weather.

components.label: HBlank-DMA scanline effects and battle-entry screen transitions
components.summary: A shared scanline-effect module double-buffers 160 per-line values and streams them by DMA0 on each HBlank (16- or 32-bit, dest reload) into a BG scroll register, with a helper that generates animated sine waves. The title clouds, intro, and many of the ~42 battle transitions use it (swirl and shuffle add per-line sine offsets to BG scroll); other transitions animate windows (WIN0) or blit to BG0. Transition choice depends on map type (normal, cave, flash-dark, water), wild vs trainer, and whether the foe's first mon is lower level than the player's lead, plus special transitions for Frontier facilities, Aqua/Magma, legendaries and Elite Four.

components.label: Player-locked camera scrolling in step with tile movement
components.summary: The field camera tracks the player object: each frame it adds the player's per-frame movement speed to a 0-15 px sub-tile offset and, when a tile boundary is crossed, shifts the map origin by one metatile, moves all object events, and redraws only the newly exposed row/column into the 32x32 tilemap ring buffer. Sprites are offset by a pan that defaults to 32 px vertically so the player sits slightly below centre. A bike pan-ahead callback exists but is unreachable. If the camera cannot move (map edge without connection) the step is treated as impassable.

components.label: Top-down three-quarter view with elevation layering
components.summary: The overworld is an orthographic top-down view with three-quarter (oblique) art: building fronts and character sprites show their south face, and depth is faked by drawing tall metatile tops on the above-sprite BG layer and by per-object elevation that selects sprite priority (bridges, multi-level areas). Battles switch to a separate staged side-on view of the two sides.

evidence.ref: three-quarter art convention of Gen-3 overworld sprites

components.label: Tile-locked stepping with turn-in-place and hold-B running
components.summary: The player and NPCs move exactly one 16 px metatile per step along four directions; input is read only between steps. Pressing a new direction while standing turns in place (a short walk-in-place animation) instead of stepping, so taps reorient. Speeds come from a per-speed table of whole-pixel step functions: walking 1 px/frame (16 frames/tile), running (B held after the Running Shoes flag, not on no-running tiles, not underwater) and surfing 2 px/frame (8 frames), currents/acro bike ~2.67 px/frame (6 frames), mach bike top speed 4 px/frame (4 frames), and an 8 px/frame speed for scripted movement. There is no acceleration except on the Mach Bike.

components.label: Per-tile collision bits, directional blocks, elevation and object collision
components.summary: Before every step the destination tile is tested in order: outside the object's wander range, the block's 2-bit collision value, map edge without connection, directional impassability from the metatile behaviour (e.g. blocked only when entering from the north), whether the camera can scroll, elevation mismatch (a 4-bit level; 0 and 15 match anything), and occupancy by another object. Special outcomes override a plain bump: walking off water onto land at a matching elevation stops surfing, jump behaviours trigger ledge hops, a Strength-boulder object gets pushed, rotating-gate puzzles and Acro Bike rails have their own codes.

components.label: One-way ledge hop over a tile
components.summary: Moving into a jump-behaviour metatile in its allowed direction plays the ledge sound and performs a scripted two-tile hop: 32 frames, 1 px/frame horizontal, with a lookup-table arc (high jump, peak 12 px) applied as a sprite y-offset only. Ledges cannot be climbed from below, which makes them one-way shortcuts back toward towns.

components.label: Behaviour tiles that take control (ice, arrows, currents, slides, mats, muddy slopes, cracked floors)
components.summary: After each step the player's current metatile behaviour is checked against an ordered table; a match takes over movement: ice and the Trick House slippery floor slip the player forward until a non-ice tile or wall; walk/arrow tiles force walking in a direction; water currents push at the faster speed; slide tiles slide; secret-base jump and spin mats animate; muddy slopes push the player back south unless moving north at Mach Bike top speed. Cracked floors in Sky Pillar and Granite Cave break after being stepped on and drop the player through unless crossed on the Mach Bike.

components.label: Mach Bike three-gear momentum
components.summary: The Mach Bike accelerates while the d-pad is held in one direction: the first step uses walking speed, the second running speed, and from the third step on it moves 4 px/frame. Releasing or turning drops speed one gear per step; hitting a wall stops dead (bonk). Top speed is required to climb muddy slopes and to cross cracked floors. Bike movement reduces the wild encounter rate to 80%. Bikes are allowed only on maps whose header permits cycling.

components.label: Acro Bike tricks (wheelie, bunny hop, side jumps, rails)
components.summary: The Acro Bike moves at a constant 6 frames/tile and has a trick state machine driven by B and the d-pad history: hold B to pop a wheelie, keep holding to bunny-hop in place or while moving, tap B with a direction to side-jump or turn-jump. Hopping crosses rail and white-rail metatiles and stepping-stone gaps that block normal movement; bumpy slopes need a wheelie.

components.label: Surf, Dive and Waterfall water traversal modes
components.summary: Surf turns the avatar into a rider on a Pokémon over water-elevation tiles at 2 px/frame and is ended by stepping onto land at a matching elevation. On deep-water tiles Dive warps to a parallel underwater map (and back up where surfacing is allowed), where running is disabled. Waterfall tiles force upward climbing when surfing with the move. Currents in the open sea push the surfer. Surf/water tiles use their own encounter table.

components.label: Bytecode event-script VM with flags, vars and specials
components.summary: World logic (NPC dialogue, cutscenes, item balls, trainers, warps, map setup) is bytecode run by a script context: one opcode byte indexes a 228-entry command table, with a 20-deep call stack, native-callback mode for waits, and 528 "special" C functions callable by id. Commands can yield (wait for message, movement, fade). Map headers carry script tables run on load, transition, resume, frame and warp-in. State lives in ~2400 bit flags (temporary, per-trainer, system, daily) and 256 16-bit vars (0x4000-0x40FF) plus special vars 0x8000+. A RAM script slot lets Mystery Event data inject scripts. Running a script locks player field controls.

components.label: Global LCG random generator with per-frame advance
components.summary: Random() steps a 32-bit LCG (multiplier 1103515245, increment 24691) and returns the high 16 bits; a second independent generator exists for some subsystems. The main generator also advances once per VBlank outside link, Frontier and recorded battles, so outcomes depend on frame timing. In the retail build the boot seed is not taken from the RTC (that code is compiled only under BUGFIX), so the state starts at 0 at power-on and is first reseeded from Timer 1 when a new game's name entry finishes.

components.label: Personality-seeded, encrypted creature records
components.summary: Each Pokémon is a 32-bit personality value plus original-trainer ID, nickname and four 12-byte substructs (growth, attacks, EVs/condition, misc) whose order is personality mod 24 and whose words are XOR-encrypted with personality ^ OT ID, guarded by a checksum. Personality alone fixes nature (mod 25), ability slot (bit 0), gender (low byte vs species gender ratio) and Wurmple's branch; personality xor OT ID decides shininess (8 in 65536). Party records add level, status and computed stats. Contest condition (cool, beauty, cute, smart, tough, sheen 0-255) is stored per mon.

components.label: Base stats + IVs + EVs + nature stat formula
components.summary: Stats are recomputed from species base stats, per-stat individual values (0-31), effort values (0-255 per stat, 510 total, gained from defeating species) and level: HP = floor((2*Base + IV + floor(EV/4)) * L / 100) + L + 10; other stats = floor((2*Base + IV + floor(EV/4)) * L / 100) + 5, then x1.1 or x0.9 if the nature raises or lowers that stat. Shedinja always has 1 HP. Level comes from total experience on the growth curve.

components.label: Turn-based party battle engine with battle-script VM and controllers
components.summary: Battles pit parties of up to six in singles, doubles (four battlers) or multi formats. Each turn every battler's controller (player input, AI, link, recorded playback, Safari, Wally tutorial) chooses FIGHT (one of four PP-limited moves), BAG, POKÉMON (switch) or RUN; actions are ordered (switches and items before moves, then by priority and speed), then each move executes as a script on a battle-script VM of 249 commands (accuracy, crit, damage, type, effects, messages, animations). End-of-turn effects (weather, status damage, leech seed, items) resolve in a fixed order. Fainted mons must be replaced; a side with no usable mon loses. Wild battles can be fled with a speed-based escape roll.

components.label: Priority-then-speed turn order with modifiers
components.summary: For two move users, higher move priority goes first; with equal priority the higher effective speed goes first and exact ties are a coin flip. Effective speed = Spe * stage ratio, doubled by Swift Swim in rain or Chlorophyll in sun, x1.1 for the player with the third badge (not in link/Frontier), halved by Macho Brace, quartered by paralysis; Quick Claw sets effective speed to UINT_MAX when the shared per-turn random value is below floor(65535*holdEffectParam/100), with a native item parameter of 20. This does not bypass move priority; two ordinary Quick Claw holders share the same activation test rather than rolling independently. Each integer division truncates at its position in the calculation.
writes: rng.state:u32 (only when equal priority and equal effective speed require a Random call)

components.label: Gen-3 damage formula
components.summary: Base damage = floor(floor(floor(A_eff * Power * (floor(2*L/5) + 2)) / D_eff) / 50), where A/D are Atk/Def for physical types or SpA/SpD for special types after stage ratios and modifiers; burn halves physical damage (not with Guts); Reflect/Light Screen halve it (2/3 in doubles with two targets); spread moves halve it in doubles; rain/sun scale Water/Fire x1.5 or x0.5; then +2. The script then multiplies by the crit multiplier (x2), Charge (x2 Electric) and Helping Hand (x1.5), applies STAB x1.5 and each defending type's effectiveness in turn, and finally a random factor of (100 - rand%16)/100 (0.85-1.00). Every step truncates, and damage is at least 1 unless immune. Crits ignore the attacker's negative and the defender's positive stat stages and the screens.

components.label: 17-type effectiveness matrix
components.summary: Moves and Pokémon carry types from 17 real types (plus ???). A move's damage is multiplied by the matrix entry for each distinct defending type in turn (so dual types stack to x4, x0.25 or x0), stored as a sparse list of (attacker, defender, x0/x0.5/x2) triples; unlisted pairs are x1. Normal and Fighting vs Ghost immunities sit after a Foresight marker so Foresight/Odor Sleuth can skip them. Levitate blocks Ground and Wonder Guard blocks any damaging move that is not super effective.

components.label: Stat stages, accuracy/evasion check and critical-hit stages
components.summary: Battle-only stat stages run -6..+6. Atk/Def/Spe/SpA/SpD use ratios (2+n)/2 for boosts and 2/(2-n) for drops (x0.25..x4). Accuracy uses the move accuracy times a separate ratio table indexed by (attacker accuracy stage - target evasion stage), then Compound Eyes x1.3, Sand Veil in sandstorm x0.8, Hustle (physical) x0.8 and BrightPowder/Lax Incense; the move hits if rand(1..100) <= result. Critical hits use a stage count (Focus Energy +2, high-crit moves +1, Scope Lens +1, Lucky Punch/Stick +2 for their species) into chances 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/3, 1/2; Battle Armor and Shell Armor prevent crits, and the tutorial battles never crit.

components.label: Persistent status ailments and volatile confusion
components.summary: One major status per mon persists outside battle: sleep (2-5 turns, cannot act), poison (1/8 max HP per turn), bad poison (n/16 growing each turn up to 15/16), burn (1/8 per turn and halves physical damage), paralysis (speed /4, 25% chance each turn to be fully paralysed) and freeze (80% chance per turn to stay frozen; fire moves thaw). Volatile confusion makes the user hit itself 50% of the time with a typeless 40-power physical attack. Status also doubles (sleep/freeze) or x1.5 (others) catch odds and enables Guts/Marvel Scale.

components.label: Passive abilities and held-item hold effects
components.summary: Every species has one or two abilities (slot picked by personality bit 0), 77 in all, and any mon can hold one item. Both are passive hooks checked at fixed points (switch-in, before/after a move, end of turn, damage calc, accuracy, speed, encounter generation): e.g. Intimidate lowers foe Atk on entry, Levitate grants Ground immunity, Swift Swim doubles speed in rain, Sitrus/Oran berries heal at low HP, Leftovers heal 1/16 per turn, Focus Band survives a KO at 1 HP 10% of the time, Choice Band x1.5 Atk, Amulet Coin doubles prize money. Several abilities also act in the overworld when the lead mon has them (encounter rate, wild level, nature sync, match-call rate).

components.label: Battle weather (rain, sun, sandstorm, hail)
components.summary: Weather is a field-wide battle state set by moves for 5 turns, permanently by Drizzle/Drought/Sand Stream abilities, or permanently from the overworld weather at battle start (rain types, sandstorm, drought). Rain boosts Water and weakens Fire x1.5/x0.5, sun the reverse, rain/sand/hail halve Solar Beam, sun makes Thunder 50% accurate, sandstorm and hail deal 1/16 max HP to non-immune types each turn, and Swift Swim/Chlorophyll/Sand Veil key off it. Cloud Nine and Air Lock suppress all weather effects.

components.label: Double and multi battle formats
components.summary: Doubles put two battlers per side. Spread moves (target both foes) deal half damage while two targets remain, screens cut damage to 2/3 instead of 1/2, AI picks a random foe as default target and adds a double-battle script that avoids hitting its partner. In Emerald the overworld can trigger doubles three ways: a double-battle trainer pair, two separate trainers spotting the player at once (if the player has two usable mons), and the Steven tag battle with an AI partner, plus Frontier multi battles.

components.label: Ball-throw capture formula with four shake checks
components.summary: Throwing a ball at a wild mon computes a = floor(catchRate * ballBonus/10 * (3*MaxHP - 2*HP) / (3*MaxHP)), x2 for sleep/freeze or x1.5 for poison/burn/paralysis. If a > 254 the catch succeeds; otherwise b = floor(1048560 / floor(sqrt(floor(sqrt(floor(16711680 / a)))))) and up to four checks Random() < b each add a shake; four passes catch the mon (shown as three shakes then success). Master Ball always catches. Trainer-owned mons cannot be caught; the Wally tutorial always succeeds.

components.label: Per-step random encounters from slot-weighted tables (with roamers and outbreaks)
components.summary: Each map may define land (12 slots), water (5), rock-smash (5) and fishing (old/good/super rod: 2/3/5 slots) tables with an encounter rate. On each step onto a grass/water/cave tile the chance is rate*16/2880, modified by bike (x0.8), White/Black Flute (x0.5/x1.5), Cleanse Tag (x2/3) and lead abilities (Stench/White Smoke x0.5, Illuminate/Arena Trap x2, Sand Veil in sandstorm x0.5); when the step changes metatile behaviour (e.g. entering grass) a 60% pre-check applies first. A slot is then rolled from fixed weights and a level from its min-max range; Repel blocks foes below the lead's level, Keen Eye/Intimidate skip low-level foes half the time, Static/Magnet Pull bias toward Electric/Steel, Synchronize copies nature 50%. A roaming Latias or Latios (1/4 when on the same map) and TV-announ…

components.label: Day Care breeding with compatibility, IV/nature inheritance and step-hatched eggs
components.summary: Two Pokémon left at the Day Care gain 1 exp per step. Every 256 steps an egg is rolled with probability equal to compatibility: 70 same species different OT, 50 same species same OT or different species different OT (or Ditto with a different OT), 20 different species same OT (or Ditto same OT), 0 if same gender, genderless, no shared egg group or Undiscovered group. The egg is the mother's (or non-Ditto parent's) base species, inherits 3 IVs from random parents, the Everstone holder's nature 50% of the time, and egg/TM moves from the father. Eggs hatch after their species' egg cycles, one cycle per 255 steps (two with Magma Armor or Flame Body in the party).

components.label: Cartridge real-time clock driving daily and per-minute world updates
components.summary: The cartridge RTC gives a day count and time (offset by the player's clock setting). Gen 3 has no visual day/night: time drives systems instead. On a day rollover the game clears daily flags and advances Dewford trends, TV shows, weather, Pokérus, the Mirage Island seed, Birch state, Frontier NPCs, the Shoal Cave item flag and the lottery number; elapsed minutes advance berry trees. Shoal Cave tide is high 09-14 and 21-02. Friendship evolutions split at 12:00 (day 12-23, night 0-11). Mirage Island appears when any party mon's low personality half matches the daily random value.

components.label: Pokémon Contests (condition judging plus five-round appeal minigame)
components.summary: Four contestants compete in one of five categories (Cool, Beauty, Cute, Smart, Tough) at Normal/Super/Hyper/Master rank. Round 1 points = main condition + (the two adjacent conditions + sheen)/2, where conditions are raised by feeding Pokéblocks made from berries. Round 2 is five appeal turns: each move has a category, hearts (up to 8) and an effect (jam others, startle, combos, order changes); using moves matching the contest category raises a 5-level applause meter and filling it grants a +60 appeal bonus (else +10). Final score = round 1 + 2 x appeal total; winners earn ribbons and a painting.

components.label: Secret bases with decorations and record-mixed rival bases
components.summary: Secret Power opens a base in marked trees, shrubs and cave walls. The player places up to 16 decorations (mats with jump/spin/sound behaviours, dolls, posters, furniture) and the base stores a party snapshot. Bases from other players arrive by record mixing (20 slots kept, registrable), appear in the world, and their owners can be battled once a day using the stored party.

components.label: Flag-selected script modules that score each move, then pick the max
components.summary: Each opponent turn every usable move starts at score 100 (unusable moves 0). The trainer's AI flags select script modules from a 32-entry table, run in bit order over every move; each module adds or subtracts points via conditionals over the real battle state (the AI sees the player's exact HP, types, ability and last move). After all modules the AI picks uniformly among the moves with the highest score. Damage queries (can this KO? is this the strongest move?) re-run the damage formula with a random factor pre-rolled per move at setup. Special flags replace move choice with an action: roamers flee unless trapped, Safari mons flee or watch, and the first-battle Zigzagoon flees at <=20 HP. Gym leaders and Elite Four use BAD_MOVE+TRY_TO_FAINT+VIABILITY (+SETUP_FIRST_TURN for some); most rou…

components.label: Rule-based trainer switching and item use
components.summary: Before move scoring, trainer AI may switch or use an item. It switches (if another healthy mon exists) when Perish Song is about to KO it, when it cannot touch a Wonder Guard foe, when a party mon absorbs the foe's last move type, or to cure a status via Natural Cure; it stays in if it has a super-effective move or raised stats; otherwise it may switch to a party mon resistant/immune to the foe's last move with 1/2 or 1/3 chance. The replacement is the mon with the best type matchup against the foe. Trainers carry up to 4 items: Full Restore below 1/4 HP, potions when below 1/4 or the heal would not overflow, status cures, X items and Guard Spec on early turns.

components.label: Nature-driven autonomous move choice (Battle Palace)
components.summary: In the Battle Palace (and Verdanturf Tent) neither side picks moves: each Pokémon's nature gives percentage odds of choosing from its Attack, Defense or Support move groups, with a different distribution once it is at or below 50% HP; a flavour line describes its mood. This turns natures into a behaviour personality, e.g. Lax: 35/10/55 healthy but 29/6/65 when hurt.

evidence.ref: pokeemerald:src/battle_gfx_sfx_util.c (palace move selection reads the likelihood table)

components.label: Contest opponent move scoring
components.summary: NPC contestants run contest-AI script modules selected by flag bits (check bad move, combos, boring/repeat, excitement, turn order, good move, erratic) that adjust four move scores starting at 100; the move is then chosen by repeatedly drawing a random move index until it lands on a top-scoring move.

components.label: Trainer sight lines, approach and forced battle
components.summary: After each player step, undefeated trainer NPCs test whether the player stands within their sight range (per-object, in tiles) straight ahead in their facing direction (or in any of the four directions for "see all" and buried trainers) with no blocking tile or object between. A spotting trainer shows an exclamation mark, walks up to the adjacent tile, the player turns to face them, and the battle script runs; disguised (tree/rock) and buried trainers reveal first. Two trainers can spot the player at once, producing a double battle if the player has two usable mons. Each trainer's flag records the defeat.

components.label: Data-driven NPC ambient movement types
components.summary: Every object event template names one of ~80 movement types, each a small per-object state machine: stand facing a direction, look around or turn between 2-3 facings, wander within a rectangular range, walk back and forth, walk a fixed 4-direction sequence, rotate, copy the player's movement (mirror or same direction), or follow scripted movement. Wanderers wait a random delay (32/64/96/128 frames), pick a random direction and step if not blocked. Up to 16 objects are live at once from 64 templates per map.

components.label: Experience yield, sharing and six growth curves
components.summary: Defeating a mon yields floor(baseExpYield * foeLevel / 7) experience, split evenly among participating healthy mons; if anyone holds Exp. Share, half goes to participants and half is split among holders. Trainer battles, traded mons (OT differs) and Lucky Egg each multiply by 1.5. Defeated species also award EVs. Level is looked up from total experience on one of six growth curves (level 100 at 600,000 to 1,640,000 exp). Level-ups recompute stats, teach level-up moves and check evolution.

components.label: Multi-trigger evolution table
components.summary: Each species lists up to five evolutions with a method and parameter: level reached, friendship >= 220 (any time, day 12-23 or night 0-11 by the RTC), trade, trade holding an item, item use (stones), level with Atk >, = or < Def, Wurmple's personality split, Nincada's Ninjask + Shedinja split (Shedinja appears in a free party slot), and beauty >= value (Feebas). An Everstone blocks evolution. Level evolutions run after battle; the player can cancel with B.

components.label: Eight-gym badge ladder to the Pokémon League
components.summary: The critical path is eight gyms in a fixed geographic order, each badge a world flag that gates the next region via HM use (badge N unlocks one field move outside battle), raises the level up to which traded mons obey (10 base; 30, 50, 70 at badges 2/4/6; all at 8), and grants hidden 10% stat boosts (Atk at badge 1, Speed at 3, Def at 5, SpA/SpD at 7) to the player's side in normal battles. After the eighth badge Victory Road leads to the Elite Four and Champion; clearing them sets the game-clear flag and opens the postgame (Battle Frontier access, National Dex, Sky Pillar etc.). Five badges also arm trainer rematches.

evidence.ref: Elite Four / Champion and postgame structure

components.label: HM field moves as world keys
components.summary: Overworld obstacles are typed locks opened by a party Pokémon knowing a field move and the matching badge: Cut trees, Flash for dark caves, Rock Smash boulders (with their own encounter table), Strength push-boulders, Surf water, Fly to visited towns (fast travel), Dive into deep water, Waterfall climbing; plus Secret Power for base spots and Teleport/Dig/Sweet Scent utilities. HMs cannot be forgotten normally, so slots on the team become a resource.

components.label: PokéNav Match Call and step-gated trainer rematches
components.summary: Registered trainers can phone the player through the PokéNav: every 10 steps, if at least 10 minutes passed since the last check, a call fires 30% of the time (60% with a Lightning Rod lead). With five badges, a rematch step counter fills to 255; after that, entering a map gives each rematchable trainer there a 31% chance to want a rematch with a stronger party, and gym leaders get rematches too.

components.label: Pokédex seen/caught collection goal (Hoenn then National)
components.summary: The Pokédex records species seen and caught; the Hoenn dex covers 202 species and the National dex (386) unlocks after the game is cleared. Completion is an optional collection goal that requires catching, evolving, breeding and trading (some species are version exclusives).

components.label: Battle Frontier postgame challenge facilities with streaks and Battle Points
components.summary: Emerald's postgame island hosts seven facilities with rule twists: Tower (straight battles; singles, doubles, multis), Dome (tournament), Palace (nature-driven moves), Arena (3-turn bouts judged on Mind, Skill and Body), Factory (rental mons), Pike (room-choice gauntlet) and Pyramid (dark maze floors with wild encounters and a restricted bag). Each challenge is 7 battles at Level 50 or Open level, opponents use smart AI, streaks are tracked up to 9999, and wins pay Battle Points from a per-facility table that grows with challenge number; Frontier Brains award silver and gold symbols. Badge stat boosts, Soul Dew and normal obedience rules are disabled there.

components.label: Single currency with level-scaled trainer prizes and shops
components.summary: Money (cap 999,999, start 3,000) is the main currency. Beating a trainer pays 4 x (level of their last party mon) x class base value (e.g. Youngster 4, Gym Leader/Elite Four 25, Champion/Rich Boy 50, default 5), x2 for a lone double-battle trainer and x2 with Amulet Coin. Money buys items at Poké Marts (sell price is half the buy price) and is halved on whiteout. Side currencies exist: Game Corner coins, Battle Points and Pokéblocks/berries.

components.label: Pocketed bag, PC item storage and 14-box Pokémon storage
components.summary: Items live in five bag pockets with fixed slot counts (Items 30, Key Items 30, Poké Balls 16, TMs/HMs 64, Berries 46), overflow goes to the PC item box, and one key item can be registered to Select. Pokémon beyond the party of six go to the PC storage system of 14 boxes x 30. The Battle Pyramid swaps in a separate 10-slot bag.

components.label: Real-time berry tree farming with watering-based yield
components.summary: Berries planted in soft soil grow through planted, sprouted, taller and flowering stages, each lasting the berry's stage duration in real hours; the fruit stage lasts four times as long before the berries fall and the tree regrows from the sprout stage (up to 10 regrowths). Watering in each stage raises yield: with w watered stages the yield is min + round((max-min) * random share of w/4). If the elapsed time exceeds 71 stage durations the tree vanishes. Berries feed Pokéblock blending (flavours map to contest conditions) and many are held battle items.

components.label: Battle health boxes and FIGHT/BAG/POKéMON/RUN command menu
components.summary: Battles show a health box per battler (name, gender, level, status, HP bar; the player's also shows HP numbers and an EXP bar) and a text box with the command menu FIGHT, BAG, POKéMON, RUN; FIGHT opens a four-move grid with PP and type. HP bars drain over frames and change colour: green above 50%, yellow above 20%, red below. Messages print through the shared text printer.

components.label: Start-menu hub (Pokédex, Pokémon, Bag, PokéNav, Trainer, Save, Option)
components.summary: Start opens a vertical menu that hubs all out-of-battle screens: Pokédex, party (with field moves and item use), bag, PokéNav (region map, condition, Match Call, ribbons), trainer card, save and options; context variants replace entries in the Safari Zone (Retire) and Battle Pyramid (Pyramid Bag, Rest/Retire). No HUD is shown during overworld play.

components.label: Context button mapping
components.summary: D-pad moves (tap to turn), A interacts with the faced tile/object or confirms, B cancels and, once the Running Shoes are owned, is held to run (Acro Bike tricks on the bike), Start opens the menu, Select uses the registered key item (bike, rod). L/R scroll lists; an option makes L act as A. Menus repeat held directions after 40 frames then every 5.

evidence.ref: A/Start/Select/L-R roles and the L=A option

components.label: Typewriter text boxes driven by scripts
components.summary: NPCs, signs and battles speak through framed text windows printed character by character at the chosen text speed (slow 8, mid 4, fast 1 frame per character); A/B advance or speed up, with scroll and wait-for-button control codes and yes/no or multichoice menus for choices. Strings use the game's own charset and placeholders for player/rival/mon names.

evidence.ref: capture:frontend:keyframes f001157..f005385 (Birch dialogue windows, typewriter mid-line frames "To unrave", "So it's")

components.label: Scripted in-engine story with rival, two villain teams and weather legendaries
components.summary: The story is told with event scripts that move NPCs, play music cues and print dialogue: the player moves to Littleroot, rescues Professor Birch, picks a starter, races a rival (Brendan/May) and the eight gyms, and crosses paths with both Team Magma and Team Aqua, whose awakening of Groudon and Kyogre creates the "abnormal" alternating weather over Sootopolis until Rayquaza is called down from Sky Pillar. Story state lives in event flags and per-area state vars.

evidence.ref: Emerald plot outline (Birch rescue, rival, Magma and Aqua, Groudon/Kyogre/Rayquaza)

components.label: Tropical Hoenn region of creatures and trainers
components.summary: A cheerful contemporary-fantasy region of islands, volcano, desert and ocean routes where people coexist with and battle alongside Pokémon; tone is adventurous and bright, with an environmental-crisis plot about land versus sea.

evidence.ref: capture:attract:keyframes f001183, f001850 (grassland/route scenery, player on bike with Pokémon)

components.label: MP2K (m4a) sequenced engine with DirectSound mixing and PSG
components.summary: Audio uses Nintendo's MusicPlayer2000 (m4a) driver: m4aSoundMain mixes up to 5 DirectSound sample voices at 13,379 Hz into both FIFOs (refilled by sound DMA) alongside the four PSG channels, from MIDI-derived sequences with voice groups, key-split tables, direct-sound samples and programmable waveforms. Four music players run at once: BGM (10 tracks), SE1 (3), SE2 (9) and SE3 (1); species cries are separate PCM tone data that duck the BGM.

evidence.ref: capture:attract+frontend audio_flags directsound_A/B true, 13379 Hz throughout

components.label: Map-header music with fades, fanfare interrupts and cry ducking
components.summary: Each map header names a BGM; a map-music state machine fades out and fades in only when the new map's track differs, and surfing/biking override tracks. Fanfares (level up, item, badge, evolution, heal...) pause the BGM for a fixed frame length then resume it, and Pokémon cries temporarily lower BGM volume. Trainer classes have encounter themes that start when spotted; battles and the title use their own tracks (the title track does not loop, which ends the title screen).

components.label: Key-sampling frame loop with reset guard
components.summary: AgbMain reads keys, checks the A+B+Start+Select chord unless soft reset is disabled, coordinates link processing, updates play time/map music and waits for VBlank. This Rev1-supported source initializes RFU, GPU managers and a heap and disables help at boot; reset also stops RFU.

components.label: Physical, edge and repeated keys with L=A remapping
components.summary: ReadKeys derives new keys before applying L=A to held/new fields. The source explicitly records that repeat compares raw input with the remapped previous held keys and never remaps newAndRepeatedKeys, so L=A repeat has a known discrepancy. Watched-key masks latch new presses for waiting callers.

components.label: Global high-word LCG also advances at VBlank

games.name: Pokémon Ruby Version

components.label: Key-sampling frame loop with reset guard
components.summary: AgbMain reads keys, checks the A+B+Start+Select chord unless soft reset is disabled, coordinates link processing, updates play time/map music and waits for VBlank. Ruby initializes the RTC and seeds its generator from it.

components.label: Physical, edge and repeated keys with L=A remapping
components.summary: ReadKeys derives new keys before applying L=A to held/new fields. The source explicitly records that repeat compares raw input with the remapped previous held keys and never remaps newAndRepeatedKeys, so L=A repeat has a known discrepancy. Watched-key masks latch new presses for waiting callers.

components.label: Global high-word LCG also advances at VBlank
components.summary: Random updates a 32-bit state using multiplier 1103515245 and increment 24691, returning the upper 16 bits. The inspected VBlank path calls Random in addition to event-specific callers; frame timing therefore affects future battle/encounter outcomes. No claim of uniform event probabilities or replay determinism follows from the recurrence alone.

components.label: Yielding bytecode and native-function script context
components.summary: RunScriptCommand switches stopped/native/bytecode modes. Bytecode dispatch runs until a handler requests a yield, the script pointer becomes null or the opcode lies beyond the command table. Native mode resumes bytecode when the callback reports completion. An initial stopped-mode guard is present.

components.label: Rotating checksummed sector save slots
components.summary: A full save increments its counter, rotates the starting sector modulo 14 and writes 14 chunks. Each chunk is placed into one of two physical slot sets selected by saveCounter%2, with ID, signature, counter and checksum in its footer. If damaged sectors are reported, the writer restores its prior counter/start index. This is source architecture, not a tested power-loss recovery campaign.

components.label: Defeat heals and warps with half-money retention
components.summary: DoWhiteOut halves the wallet using integer division, heals the party, resets overworld state and warps to the last healing location.

components.label: Turn-first grid movement and gated B-running
components.summary: The movement classifier distinguishes idle, turn-in-place and moving from input direction and current movement state. Moving tests collisions before dispatch; surfing uses a fast step and held B requests running only after FLAG_SYS_B_DASH and a terrain permission check. Underwater mode excludes running.

components.label: Terrain-selected movement overrides
components.summary: The forced-movement dispatch maps terrain predicates to slip, forced cardinal walking, currents, slides, waterfall and mat actions. Ruby also lists muddy slopes. These are source-supported modes; exact speeds, stopping distances and puzzle timing remain to be extracted.

components.label: Per-pixel camera movement with metatile streaming
components.summary: CameraUpdate runs an optional callback, accumulates movement offsets modulo 16 and moves/redraws map slices when a cell boundary is crossed. It updates object events and global camera-pixel offsets alongside tilemap streaming. Ruby also updates rotating-gate puzzles and berry sparkle flags.

components.label: Two-layer metatiles distributed over hardware background planes
components.summary: DrawMetatile writes four bottom and four top tile entries per metatile, choosing target background buffers by layer type and inserting transparent entries where needed. The inspected split case differs in exact buffer numbering between Ruby and FRLG; only the compositional behavior is shared here. Source-specific buffer references remain in citations.

components.label: Integer IV/EV/level/nature statistic calculation
components.summary: For ordinary species maxHP is floor((2*baseHP+IV+floor(EV/4))*level/100)+level+10; Shedinja instead gets 1. Other stats add 5 before a nature modifier. Current HP adjusts by the change in maxHP when nonzero, rather than unconditionally refilling. The source records an HP underflow edge behind an optional BUGFIX guard, which is not assumed enabled for a matching cartridge build.

components.label: Move priority before adjusted speed and item effects
components.summary: GetWhoStrikesFirst compares move-priority brackets, then adjusted speed; equal speed within equal priority uses Random()&1. Weather abilities double speed, the third badge can multiply player speed by 110/100 outside link battles, Macho Brace halves it and paralysis divides by four. A Quick Claw trigger sets adjusted speed to UINT_MAX but still does not cross a higher move-priority bracket. Inference: speed control and priority are distinct tactical operators, not measured player skills.

components.label: Flag-selected move-score scripts and random best-score choice
components.summary: Setup initializes each move to score 100, zeros unusable moves and samples simulated damage factors as 100-(Random()%16). Active AI-flag modules process all move indices; selection chooses among maximum-scoring candidates using RNG, with explicit flee/watch exceptions. Ruby routes first-battle/safari/roamer flags separately.

components.label: Rule-table evolution with mode and held-item checks
components.summary: GetEvolutionTargetSpecies scans species evolution methods for normal, trade or item-use modes, checking level, friendship, stats, beauty and personality conditions. The prevent-evolve hold effect blocks real evolution but permits item-check mode. Friendship day/night branches call RTC and use 12..23 versus 0..11 hours respectively; these source-defined intervals should not be silently relabeled by ordinary daylight assumptions.

components.label: Version-specific bag pocket capacities
components.summary: Constants allocate separate item, key-item, ball, TM/HM and berry pockets. Ruby uses 20/20/16/64/46 slots and 50 PC-item slots. These are storage capacities, not catalogues or a claim that all items are currently unlocked.

components.label: Six-creature party and four move slots
components.summary: Independent local constants set party size to six and a creature move-set size to four. This is the bounded state layout used by party and AI systems; it is not evidence that every battle places all six creatures on screen or permits four simultaneous active combatants.

components.label: Weighted encounter slots and actual Ruby starter-route data
components.summary: The source selects a land slot by Random()%total against cumulative thresholds; its data specifies twelve weights [20,20,10,10,10,10,5,5,4,4,1,1]. Route101_Ruby has encounter-rate parameter 20 and the explicit per-slot species/levels in the table. This rate parameter is not a direct percent chance per player step; the runtime tests terrain transitions and encounter-rate logic first.

components.label: Progress-gated start-menu destinations
components.summary: The ordinary field menu adds Pokédex and Pokémon only after their system flags, plus Bag, Player, Save, Options and Exit. PokéNav is also inserted after its own acquisition flag. Safari/link routines construct other lists, so the menu depends on session context.

components.label: Mode-0/1 frontend video with phase-limited evidence
components.summary: The existing 9000-frame attract/frontend capture recorded mode 0 and mode 1, alpha/brightness effects, sprites and hardware windows. Counts are capture observations and do not show how often these techniques occur across a complete playthrough. Bitmap modes were not observed in this run; absence in this frontend sample is not absence from the entire ROM.

components.label: Observed per-line scroll DMA writes
components.summary: The baseline capture identifies HBlank DMA target ch0->0x04000014 (bg_scroll). This distinguishes BG1 scroll modulation from a mode-7/per-line affine claim. CPU palette-raster activity was also flagged; attribution to individual scenes needs telemetry/keyframe alignment.

components.label: m4a software mixer and observed dual-DirectSound rate
components.summary: AgbMain initializes m4a and the VBlank path runs m4aSoundMain. Baseline telemetry records DirectSound FIFO-rate observations at 13379 Hz; this is the hardware delivery rate in the capture, not the 16 kHz WAV export rate. The source/capture establish engine technology without assigning musical genre from model recall.

components.label: Map-music queue waits for stop and fanfare completion
components.summary: MapMusicMain handles current/next music and restart/fade-in states. Transition states 6 and 7 wait for both BGM stopped and inactive fanfare before starting the next map track, so the queue preserves a temporary jingle rather than immediately overwriting it. Explicit parameters for every map theme were not inventoried here.

components.label: Introductory human presenter and text-panel staging
components.summary: The directly inspected frontend frame shows a front-facing human sprite in a light coat on a simple platform/background. A large empty bordered dialogue panel occupies the lower screen. Only visible staging is asserted; model captions sometimes misname presenters, and the full plot was not read.

components.label: Clock-set-gated daily and minute updates
components.summary: DoTimeBasedEvents runs only once the system-clock-set flag is present, calculating local time then daily and minute updates. Daily handling requires nondecreasing day count and resets daily flags plus several named world systems; positive elapsed minutes advance berry trees. Negative clock changes are not silently treated as elapsed growth.

components.label: Elapsed-time crop growth and reset after long absence
components.summary: BerryTreeTimeUpdate advances eligible trees by elapsed minutes, potentially through several stages; harvested-stage duration is multiplied by four. If elapsed minutes are at least a species-stage duration times 71, the tree is reset instead. Watering/yield formulas and exact per-berry times remain to be mined.

components.label: Three-index bike acceleration state
components.summary: MachBikeTransition_TrySpeedUp dispatches a speed callback indexed by bikeFrameCounter and increments that index until two after unblocked movement. It derives bikeSpeed as counter+(counter>>1); collision or forbidden facing invokes slowdown or stops. Exact frame durations and movement units were not inferred from speed enum names.

sourceReferences: https://github.com/pret/pokeruby @ 5784633ce4ef7ade1a7f2d2d0c288e3d5e6cdd7f; ruby_rev2.sha1 matches the local indexed ROM SHA1. Actual matching build not run.
